title: NPV by start year from a benefit stream

blocks.text: The capstone's practice utility (a fictional one) has a finance team that forecasts benefits differently from GridCap. Instead of one benefit in the start year, each project earns a **stream**: one amount per year of service, starting in the year **after its last year of work**, and every amount is smaller by a factor $`(1 - \delta_i)`$ for each year the project starts later than its own earliest start. Your milestone-3 job is the coefficient table the model will use: the NPV of every project for every start year in its window.

For project $`i`$ with cost profile $`c_{i,0}, \dots, c_{i,d_i-1}`$ ($k, $`d_i`$ years of work), earliest start $`e_i`$, benefit stream $`b_{i,0}, b_{i,1}, \dots`$ and decay $`\delta_i`$, started in year $`t`$, with the plan's first year $`y_0`$ and rate $`r`$:

items: `npv(project, forecast, start, years, rate)`: the formula above, as a float. `years` is the snapshot's list of plan years; `years[0]` is $`y_0`$. `discount` is given.
`npv_table(snapshot, forecast)`: `{(project id, t): whole $k}` for every $`t`$ from `earliest` to `latest`, each value rounded to the nearest whole $k (`math.floor(v + 0.5)`).

blocks.text: The ideas come from lesson 7.2.4 (shift the cash flow to the start, discount every start to one date, count benefits to the end of the asset's life and not to the end of the plan) and lesson 7.2.1 (present value). The tests use their own small portfolio; `snapshot["projects"][i]` has `cost`, `earliest` and `latest`, and `forecast[i]` has `benefits` (a list) and `decay`.

cases.says: the table has one whole-$k entry for each start in each window, and a project with costs only, started in the first plan year, is worth minus its discounted costs
the whole table matches the reference, with benefits that fall after the plan's last year still counted
every start is valued on the first plan year, so a later start of the same cash flow is worth less
benefits begin in the year after the last year of work
the decay counts the years of delay past the project's own earliest start, not past the plan's first year
a negative NPV is rounded to the nearest whole $k, not cut toward zero

origin.section: NPV by Start Year Is One Cash Flow, Shifted and Discounted to One Date

concepts: start-year NPV coefficients from a benefit stream, every start discounted to the plan's first year
